ANNEX.text:
IT BULLETIN # ${ctx.seed * (3 + ctx.siteYear) % 420}
FROM: FACILITIES

The records room lock has been reset AGAIN and I am NOT posting the number, this time.

You're going to have to work for it. Just remember that the combination is built the way it has always been built: the year the slab was poured +  the impound number of the pen that will not stay shut.

Two digits each, stitched together.

If you do not know both halves you have no business in that room.

- ${c.custodian}
ANNEX.title: IT Bulletin: PEN

ANNEX.text:
[EMERGENCY PROTOCOL MEMO]

DO NOT USE THE POUR YEAR. The architectural shift has desynchronized the locks.

The new override protocol is the elapsed HOURS since incident, followed by the OPEN PEN.

Two digits each, in that exact order. Watch the clock. Do not get trapped.
ANNEX.title: PEN + HOUR Variant

ANNEX.text:
[TORN FROM A LOGBOOK, FILED IN THE ANNEX BY MISTAKE]

People keep asking facilities for the gate combo. It has always been this: the requisition number, then the open pen. Two digits each, in that order.

Stop copying this into the annex ledger. It is not annex business.
ANNEX.title: Misfiled Combo Note

ARCHIVE.text:
[PAGES TURN, THEN CLOSE BREATHING]

...the codes were never to keep us out.
The records lock is the pour year and the open pen, two digits each, and I am saying it out loud onto tape because paper here gets reclassified and I have watched it happen.

[CLICK]
ARCHIVE.title: PEN Tape
Burn Order

ARCHIVE.text:
[STATIC, FAST FOOTSTEPS]

...they changed it. The year doesn't work anymore. 
The building knows how long we've been in here.
It's the hours.
Hours and the pen.

[CLICK]
ARCHIVE.title: HOUR Tape

INCINERATOR.text:
[HANDWRITTEN NOTE]

IT IS THE POUR AND THE PEN.
TWO DIGITS EACH.
IN THAT ORDER.

STOP ASKING.

P.S. PLEASE STOP BRINGING YOUR SEALED BOXES DOWN HERE. WE HAVE NO MORE ROOM LEFT TO BURN THEM.
INCINERATOR.title: Angry Note

INCINERATOR.text:
SCRAP INTAKE #${ctx.seed}

ITEM: Original boiler plate cut out of gallery 1 today.
DESCRIPTION: Foundry stamp on the back reads ${year}, same as the slab, and it went in before the walls did. Logged for melt, but I did not melt it. I can't.

It won't melt.
INCINERATOR.title: Scrap Intake #1

CHECKPOINT.text:
[OFFICE MEMO]

Stop coming to the gate for the records number. Nobody here has it because nobody anywhere has it.

The last three people who wanted it went to the annex to be told and one of them is still there.
CHECKPOINT.title: Irritated Memo

CHECKPOINT.text:
REQUISITION FORM 44-B — FACILITIES

ITEM: Replacement gasket, Pen ${pen} filtration line
REQ #: ${REQ}
STATUS: DENIED (insufficient justification)
RESUBMITTED: 3 times

Note from reviewer: "Stop requesting this. The gasket is fine. You are not fine."

[ Attach REQ # to Form 12-A before resubmission ]
CHECKPOINT.title: Requisition Slip 44-B

CHECKPOINT.text:
[PHOTOGRAPH]

A commissioned brass plaque, mounted inside lane 1, unpolished since installation.

"EST ${year}"

The plaque is the only date on site that has never been revised or redacted.
CHECKPOINT.title: Plaque Photo

CHECKPOINT.text:
[TAPED DIRECTLY TO THE KEYPAD]

Combo is the REQ number then your pen number. Two digits each.

Stop asking me. I am not doing this again.

- FACILITIES
CHECKPOINT.title: Checkpoint Sticky Note

CHECKPOINT.text:
[POSTED INSIDE THE GATEHOUSE, HANDWRITTEN]

Today's requisition number, so I stop getting asked: ${REQ}.

Do not call facilities again about this. Do not write it on the wall this time either.
CHECKPOINT.title: Gatehouse Requisition Note

MAINTENANCE.text:
KEY CABINET AUDIT
FROM: ${c.custodian}

Every key accounted for.

The records room is not on this list because it does not take a key, it takes the sum of this equation: the year of the pour and the pen standing open, two digits each.

I have never once written the answer down and I am not starting now
MAINTENANCE.title: Key Audit

MAINTENANCE.text:
SHIFT CLOCK MALFUNCTION REPORT

The punch clock has read hour ${ctx.hours} for three consecutive shifts now. Maintenance confirms the mechanism is intact and ticking normally.

It is simply refusing to advance past ${ctx.hours}.

We have started counting shifts on paper instead. Nobody has said why out loud.
MAINTENANCE.title: Shift Clock

MAINTENANCE.text:
REQUISITION LOG, WEEKLY TOTALS

OPEN REQUESTS CARRIED OVER: 1

THIS WEEK'S NUMBER: ${REQ}

NOTE FROM FACILITIES: We reuse the same number until the request is closed. This one has never been closed.
MAINTENANCE.title: Requisition Log

IMPOUND.text:
PROPERTY TAG: PEN #${pen}1

ITEM: Office chair, one (1) caster missing.

NOTES: No matter where it is goes, it comes back to its pen by morning.

We've stopped chasing it; the fence holds.

- ${c.custodian}
IMPOUND.title: Office Chair PEN

IMPOUND.text:
IMPOUND LEDGER, FINAL PAGE

Hour ${hrs}: ${c.custodian} logged IN one (1) personal effect belonging to ${c.lead}.

Hour ${hrs}: ${c.custodian} logged OUT.

There is no second entry. The gate to pen ${pen} has been ajar since.
IMPOUND.title: Lost ledger

IMPOUND.text:
INTAKE TAG #${ctx.seed}

LOGGED: Hour ${hrs}.

This pen was scheduled for a routine check every six hours. Six hours have passed one hundred and forty times without a single missed entry.

No one on staff remembers assigning the check to anyone.
IMPOUND.title: Intake Tag

CLINIC.text:
[DISCHARGE NOTE, RETURNED UNDELIVERABLE]

PATIENT: ${c.lost}
FORWARDING ADDRESS AS GIVEN BY PATIENT: "Pen ${pen}. It's the one that won't shut. Leave it."

Patient gave this address on intake, before the pen was even logged as open.
CLINIC.title: Discharge Note

BOARDROOM.text:
[POLAROID PHOTO]: A concrete slab being poured.

WRITTEN ON BACK:  "To New Beginnings", ${year}
BOARDROOM.title: Pour Photo

DEFAULT.text:
[TORN CALENDAR PAGE]

Someone has been crossing out hours instead of days. The count currently reads ${hrs}, underlined three times.

Below it, in different handwriting: "that's not how long we've been here."
DEFAULT.title: Torn Calendar
